name: ramuz-skills
description: Curated Claude skills for the Perseo quant stack — drawn from superpowers + mattpocock-skills.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for ramuz-skills:

- These skills are written generically and reference some Claude Code tool and subagent names. When running under Kimi Code, translate them as follows.
- When a skill says to ask the user, ask clarifying questions, ask one question at a time, present options, or wait for the user's choice, call Kimi Code's `AskUserQuestion` tool. Do not render those choices as plain assistant text unless `AskUserQuestion` is unavailable or the session is in auto-permission mode. (Some skills, e.g. `experiment-loop`, already call `AskUserQuestion` by name — no translation needed.)
- For `AskUserQuestion`, provide 1 question with 2-4 concrete options when possible. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with `(Recommended)`.
- When a skill refers to `TodoWrite`, use Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- When a skill says `Task tool (general-purpose)`, "dispatch a `general-purpose` subagent", or you fill one of the `Subagent (general-purpose):` prompt templates, call Kimi Code's `Agent` tool with a Kimi subagent type. Never pass `general-purpose` as `subagent_type` — it is a Claude Code agent type.
- For implementation, code review, spec review, quality review, and filled subagent prompt templates, call `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"`, paste the fully filled prompt into `prompt`, and provide a short `description`. Local templates: implementer `subagent-driven-development/implementer-prompt.md`; task/quality review `subagent-driven-development/task-reviewer-prompt.md` and `re-review-prompt.md`; spec review `write-specs/spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md`; plan review `writing-plans/plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md`; code review `requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md`.
- For read-only codebase exploration that would take several searches, use `Agent` with `subagent_type: "explore"`.
- For read-only planning or architecture design, use `Agent` with `subagent_type: "plan"`.
- Keep dependent subagent steps sequential. Use multiple `Agent` calls, or `run_in_background: true` only when the work is independent and background agents are available. Never dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (they conflict).
- The `research` skill spawns a background research agent — use `Agent` with `run_in_background: true`.
- `subagent-driven-development` says to specify the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent; pass it via the `Agent` call's model field where Kimi supports it.
- When a skill refers to the `Skill` tool, use Kimi Code's native `Skill` tool. Only model-invocable skills can be reached via `Skill`; the user-only skills (`chat-to-spec`, `experiment-loop`, `grill-with-docs`, `implement`, `to-tickets`, `wayfinder`) are reachable only by slash command.
- Use Kimi Code's `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `FetchURL`, `WebSearch`, and MCP tools by their actual exposed names.
- When a skill asks to search file contents, use `Grep`; when it asks to find files by path or pattern, use `Glob`; when it asks to fetch a URL, use `FetchURL`; when it asks to search the web, use `WebSearch`.

interface.shortDescription: Curated development skills for the Perseo quant stack
interface.longDescription: Personal, curated skills for work on the Perseo quant trading stack. Covers research, spec/ticket flows, TDD, systematic debugging, planning, subagent-driven development, domain modeling, and a canonical new-feature skill that routes to the right skill at each phase.
